subject: Adjusting dedicated GPU commit ahead of renewal - phased add proposal
messages:
From: Avery Malone <avery@nimbus-robotics.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: adjust dedicated GPU commit ahead of renewal
Cc: procure@nimbus-robotics.com

Hi Karthik / Vanessa,

Hope you both had a good weekend. Quick note from procurement — our Q2 usage spiked sharply after the new perception model went live. Summary:
- Week-over-week inference token volume up ~2.5x vs forecast
- Average sequence length increased from 384 -> 610 for the new workflows
- Sustained utilization on our dedicated pool reported at ~82% (P95 window) which is starting to impact tail latency for our customers

Our renewal is in 6 weeks and we want to avoid a mid-contract outage. Can Redwood provide a proposal to: 1) increase our committed GPU count to cover the new baseline, and 2) suggest a phased ramp that minimizes up-front commit cost?

Attached is our utilization snapshot for Q2 (util_report_q2.pdf). Key constraints: finance prefers a two-stage add (minimal initial commit, top-up if usage persists), while infra wants the change to be effective before the next product sprint in mid-August.

Ask: can you send a short recommendation (capacity + pricing + timeline) by Tue 21 Jul EOD? We can sign a short addendum if the numbers look reasonable. PO reference: PO-98531.

Thanks,
Avery Malone
Head of Infrastructure Procurement
Nimbus Robotics

--
Nimbus Robotics | Building perception for autonomous logistics

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Avery Malone <avery@nimbus-robotics.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: adjust dedicated GPU commit ahead of renewal

Hi Avery — thanks for the context and the util snapshot. We ran a quick pass with the infra team and sketched two pragmatic options that balance latency risk and finance flexibility. High-level notes first:
- The utilization and sequence-length shift you reported aligns with a ~45-55% increase in token-hours per GPU for your current shapes.
- At sustained 80%+ utilization, queueing increases P95 latency sharply; adding capacity now will avoid customer-impacting tail effects.

Suggested approaches (short):
A) Phased add (recommended for finance-friendly path)
  - Immediate: +4 A100-equivalent GPUs (priority placement in your existing dedicated pool) — covers short-term headroom and reduces P95 latency risk while you validate traffic change for 4 weeks.
  - If utilization persists above 70% after 4 weeks: add additional +4 GPUs (total +8).
  - Pricing: we can offer a 9-month prorated add at the existing committed rate for the first tranche, with a 12% discount on the second tranche if you sign the full +8 within 30 days of tranche-1 activation.

B) One-time spike buffer (recommended for product-fast path)
  - Immediate +8 GPUs with a 6-month ramp credit structure to reduce short-term cash outlay.

Operational items we need from you to finalize:
- Traffic split by model (heavy -> batch vs interactive) and expected 8-week ramp plan
- Any sequence-length distribution samples or heavy prompt examples

I attached a capacity/price mapping sheet (commit_matrix_v3.xlsx) with the two options, rough cost math, and a proposed timeline that gets tranche-1 live within 7 business days of signature.

If you’re available, I propose a 30-min sync tomorrow to walk the exact numbers and get verbal buy-in. Otherwise I can convert the attached into a formal addendum and route for signature.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Account Lead, Dedicated Services
Redwood Inference

On Sun, 19 Jul 2026 at 09:12 Avery Malone <avery@nimbus-robotics.com> wrote:
> (original message and util_report_q2.pdf attached)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: adjust dedicated GPU commit ahead of renewal (internal)

Internal notes for the addendum we should propose:

1) Capacity plan
  - Tranche 1: +4 A100-eq (immediately provisioned; 7 business days SLA for placement)
  - Tranche 2: +4 A100-eq (conditional top-up after 28 days if avg util > 70%)

2) Economics
  - Keep base rate same for tranche-1 prorated months; tranche-2 gets an incentive (12% off list) if they commit to full 12-month term for the +8.
  - Offer a 30-day opt-out window on tranche-2 if they fail to reach utilization threshold (so they aren't locked into the second tranche if usage drops).

3) Operational risk mitigation
  - Auto-fallback policy: route 10% of low-priority traffic to burst pool to preserve tail latency for high-priority requests in case of sudden spikes.
  - KV cache warming plan: we'll pre-warm top models during ramp to reduce cold-KV pressure.

4) Docs & sign-off
  - Addendum language: effective on signature; tranche-2 conditional on usage audit (we provide weekly utilization report).
  - HubSpot note: add deal NR-2026-070, set renewal trigger and add internal tasks.

I'll draft the addendum text and suggested DocuSign envelope. Vanessa, can you review the SLA language for provisioning SLA and placement constraints?

Ben
Ben Carter | Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Avery Malone <avery@nimbus-robotics.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procure@nimbus-robotics.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: adjust dedicated GPU commit ahead of renewal

Karthik / Ben / Vanessa — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear options. Nimbus prefers the phased approach (A). We agree to:
- Sign tranche-1 (+4 A100-eq) immediately and target activation within 7 business days.
- Commit to evaluating utilization for 28 days; if avg util >70% we will move forward with tranche-2 (+4).
- We accept the tranche-2 incentive (12% off) and the opt-out window as spelled out.

Please send the addendum and DocuSign link. PO: PO-98531 will be referenced on the signature. We aim to have tranche-1 live before Aug 10 product sprint.

Avery Malone
Head of Infrastructure Procurement
Nimbus Robotics
